title: Athens Beyond the Rock: Neighbourhoods, Marble and the Saronic Light

bestPeriod.window: Late March-mid May & late September-early November
bestPeriod.avoid: July-August, 38°C on unshaded marble, the Acropolis closes midday in heatwaves, and half of Exarchia and Pangrati shuts for August.
bestPeriod.raw: Late March-mid May & late September-early November

accommodation.note: Boutique double, per-person share, Koukaki or Plaka fringe

food.note: Mezedopoleio dinner €18-28, souvlaki €4-5, one €50 tasting dinner

transport.note: Airport metro both ways, 5-day urban ticket, Sounion coach or Aegina ferry

activities.note: Acropolis €30, Acropolis Museum, NAM, Benaki, Kerameikos

profile.difficultyNote: 2-8-11 km a day; Acropolis, Filopappou and Lycabettus supply about 300 m of ascent between them, all on polished, slippery rock.

gatewayAirport: ATH, Eleftherios Venizelos; Metro Line 3 to Syntagma/Monastiraki 40 min (€9), X95 express bus to Syntagma 60-90 min (€5.50)
summary: Most people give Athens 36 hours and see one hill. A week lets the city separate into its actual parts: the archaeological core, the 19th-century neoclassical spine from Syntagma to Omonia, and the living neighbourhoods, Koukaki, Pangrati, Exarchia, Kypseli, where Athenians actually eat, argue and drink. This itinerary front-loads the Acropolis at first slot, then spends real time on the things people skip: the National Archaeological Museum's bronzes, Byzantine Athens, the SNFCC's Renzo Piano park, and the Saronic light at Sounion. Walking is short-distance but relentlessly uphill and downhill on marble that has been polished by two thousand years of feet.

itinerary.title: Arrival, Plaka and the first hill
itinerary.morning: Metro Line 3 in from ATH (€9), drop bags in Koukaki, then coffee at **Little Tree Book Café**, Kavalloti 2, under the museum.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk **Anafiotika**, the Cycladic quarter built by 19th-century Naxian and Anafiot masons under the north cliff, then down through Plaka to the **Roman Agora** (€8) and the octagonal **Tower of the Winds** (Andronicus of Cyrrhus, 1st century BC).
itinerary.evening: Sunset from **Filopappou Hill** (free, 20 min up) for the profile view of the Acropolis, then dinner at **Karamanlidika tou Fani**, Sokratous 1, for cured meats and cheese; €22-30pp.
itinerary.dayStats: 6.3 km, 110 m ascent; Metro Line 3 €9; Roman Agora 08:00-17:00; Filopappou open dawn to dusk.

itinerary.title: Acropolis at 08:00, then the museum
itinerary.morning: **Acropolis, first slot at 08:00** (€30, hourly slots, 15 minutes' grace either side). Go up the west ramp, do the Propylaia and Parthenon before the 09:00 cohort arrives, then the Erechtheion and the Belvedere. Descend by the south slope past the **Theatre of Dionysus** and the **Odeon of Herodes Atticus** (both on the Acropolis ticket).
itinerary.afternoon: **Acropolis Museum** (€15 summer / €10 winter, Dionysiou Areopagitou 15), the top-floor Parthenon gallery is oriented to the actual building, and the glass floor over the excavated Roman neighbourhood is the best part of the ground level.
itinerary.evening: **Mani Mani**, Falirou 10 (Peloponnesian Mani cooking, book 3-5 days, €30-40pp), then a rooftop drink at **Couleur Locale**, Normanou 3.
itinerary.dayStats: 7.1 km, 180 m ascent; Acropolis 08:00-20:00 summer, to 17:00 winter; Acropolis €30, museum €15.

itinerary.title: The Agora, Kerameikos and Psyrri
itinerary.morning: **Ancient Agora** (€10), the reconstructed Stoa of Attalos museum and the Temple of Hephaestus, the best-preserved Doric temple anywhere, standing complete because it served as a church until 1834.
itinerary.afternoon: **Kerameikos** (€8) for the cemetery road and the Dipylon Gate, then walk Ermou east and into **Psyrri**'s workshop lanes and street art around Sarri and Agiou Dimitriou.
itinerary.evening: **Ta Karamanlidika** or, better, **Nolan**, Voulis 31-33 (Greek-Japanese, book 5-10 days, €40-55pp). Late drinks in **Monastiraki** at Six d.o.g.s, Avramiotou 6-8.
itinerary.dayStats: 8.4 km, 70 m ascent; Metro Line 1/3 Monastiraki; Agora 08:00-20:00 summer; Kerameikos 08:30-15:30 winter.

itinerary.title: Cape Sounion day trip
itinerary.morning: KTEL orange coach from **Mavromateon terminal** (Pedion tou Areos) down the Athens Riviera through Glyfada and Lagonisi, about 1h45, ~€7. Sit on the right for the Saronic coast.
itinerary.afternoon: **Temple of Poseidon at Sounion** (€10, 09:30 to sunset), Doric, 444 BC, 15 columns standing on the headland; find Byron's carved signature on the north-east pillar. Lunch at **Syrtaki** below the site.
itinerary.evening: Stay for sunset over the Saronic, the reason the coach schedule exists, then the last bus back around 19:00-20:00. Late dinner in **Pangrati** at **Kalamaki Kolonaki** or **Colibri**, Empedokleous 9.
itinerary.dayStats: 3.5 km walked; coach 1h45 each way, ~€14 return; temple €10; sunset 19:00-20:30 in shoulder season.

itinerary.title: National Archaeological Museum, Exarchia, Kypseli
itinerary.morning: **National Archaeological Museum**, Patission 44 (€12 summer / €6 winter), three hours minimum. The Mycenaean gold, the Antikythera Mechanism, the Artemision Bronze and the Cycladic figurines are the spine of the collection.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk into **Exarchia** for the bookshops around Themistokleous and Plateia Exarcheion, then up **Strefi Hill** for the city's least touristed view. Continue north to **Kypseli** and the restored **Dimotiki Agora Kypselis** market hall on Fokionos Negri.
itinerary.evening: **Oikonomou**, Troon 41 in Ano Petralona, a genuine old-school taverna with the day's pots on display; €18-25pp, cash preferred, no bookings.
itinerary.dayStats: 9.2 km, 90 m ascent; Metro Line 1 Victoria; NAM 13:00-20:00 Tue, 08:30-15:30 Wed-Mon in winter.

itinerary.title: Byzantine Athens, Benaki and the SNFCC
itinerary.morning: **Byzantine and Christian Museum**, Vasilissis Sofias 22 (€8) and the **Benaki Museum of Greek Culture**, Koumpari 1 (€12), the Benaki's Ottoman-era interiors and the folk-costume floor are the underrated part.
itinerary.afternoon: Tram or the free SNFCC shuttle from Syntagma to the **Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center** at Kallithea (free), Renzo Piano's canopy, the National Library reading room, the Great Lawn, and the lighthouse deck for the Saronic view.
itinerary.evening: Eat in Pangrati: **Seychelles** (Keramikou 49, Metaxourgeio) or **Mavro Provato**, Arrianou 31-33 in Pangrati, for mezedes; €25-35pp, book 3-5 days.
itinerary.dayStats: 7.6 km; tram line 6 or free shuttle; SNFCC grounds 06:00-00:00; Benaki closed Tuesdays.

itinerary.title: Market morning and departure
itinerary.morning: **Varvakios Agora** on Athinas, the meat and fish halls at 08:00, the spice and olive stalls opposite, and a bowl of *patsas* at **Papandreou** inside the hall if you have the nerve.
itinerary.afternoon: Souvlaki at **Kostas**, Pentelis 5 (one shop, one recipe, closes when the meat runs out), then Metro Line 3 from Syntagma to ATH.
itinerary.dayStats: 4.1 km; Varvakios 07:00-15:00, closed Sundays; airport metro 40 min, €9; allow 2 h at ATH.

accommodationStrategy.name: Coco-Mat Athens BC
accommodationStrategy.description: Two minutes from the Acropolis Museum on the quiet south side, so the 08:00 Acropolis slot is a ten-minute walk uphill. Rooftop with a direct Parthenon view, and Koukaki's café strip on Drakou is a better breakfast option than anything in Plaka. €150-210 double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Perianth Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: A restored 1930s modernist block with commissioned Greek art, a bakery downstairs and immediate access to Psyrri and the Agora. Right for a trip weighted toward evenings out. €180-250.

accommodationStrategy.name: Athens Was
accommodationStrategy.description: On the pedestrianised archaeological promenade, mid-century Greek design, rooms with sightlines to the south slope. Pricier per night but eliminates all transit on the two Acropolis days. €190-270.

logistics.connectivity: Full EU roaming and excellent 5G. The Metro has coverage throughout. Offline maps are worth having for Anafiotika, where the lanes defeat routing.
logistics.emergency: 112 unified; 166 ambulance, 100 police, 199 fire. Tourist police on 1571. Evangelismos is the central hospital with English-speaking staff. EU/EHIC applies.
logistics.weather: The **meltemi**, a dry northerly, blows July-September and can cancel Aegina hydrofoils at force 6+ while leaving the city merely windy. Heatwaves now routinely trigger **midday Acropolis closures (typically 12:00-17:00)** announced same-morning by the culture ministry. Winter brings brief but heavy rain and the marble becomes dangerously slick.
logistics.bookingWindows: Acropolis 1-3 weeks on hhticket.gr, choosing the 08:00 slot; Nolan and Seychelles 5-10 days; Mani Mani and Mavro Provato 3-5 days; Sounion coaches are walk-on; Aegina ferries book same-day except summer weekends.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are near-universal since the tax reforms, but neighbourhood tavernas, the Varvakios stalls and Kostas are cash-friendlier. Tip 5-10%. Bread and cover charges of €0.50-1.50 per head are standard and legal.
logistics.transportRules: Validate the Ath.ena ticket at the gate and again on buses; inspectors work Line 3 and the X95. **Urban tickets do not cover the airport**, you need the €9 airport product or the €20 three-day tourist ticket. Metro Line 3 to the airport runs only every 30 minutes, so check the departure board rather than assuming turn-up-and-go.
logistics.permits: Greece's **climate-resilience levy** replaced the old hotel tax: roughly €1.50, €10 per room per night depending on category and season, charged at the property. Archaeological sites ban tripods, drones and large bags; the Acropolis prohibits food and refuses entry with selfie sticks. Free-admission days at state sites fall on 6 March, 18 April, 18 May, the last weekend of September, 28 October, and the first Sunday of each month from November to March.
logistics.health: Tap water in central Athens is potable. Real hazards are heatstroke on unshaded sites, polished marble underfoot at the Acropolis and Filopappou, and pickpocketing on the Line 3 airport trains and around Omonia. Wear grip soles, not sandals, on the Rock.

proTips: Book the **08:00 Acropolis slot** and go straight to the Parthenon's east end. By 09:30 the cruise cohorts land and the Propylaia becomes a bottleneck for the rest of the day.

The old €30 five-day multi-site state ticket **was discontinued in April 2025**, do not buy a "combined ticket" from a reseller assuming it is the government one. Verify what a package actually includes before paying a premium.
In summer, check the culture ministry's morning announcement for **midday Acropolis heat closures** before setting out; the site now regularly shuts 12:00-17:00 on red-warning days.
State museums and sites are **free on the first Sunday of each month from November to March**, the National Archaeological Museum on such a day is the single best free thing in Europe.
Take the **X95 bus back to the airport**, not the metro, if your flight is before 07:00 or after 23:30, it runs 24 hours and costs €5.50 against a €40 taxi.
Sit on the **right-hand side of the Sounion coach** going out for the coastal views, and buy the return leg ticket on arrival at Sounion so you are not standing in the sunset queue.
Eat in **Pangrati and Ano Petralona**, not Plaka: same money buys a different quality of meal, and the walk to Plateia Varnava from the Acropolis is twenty minutes downhill.
The **SNFCC runs a free shuttle bus** from Syntagma every half hour, it saves the tram and drops you at the canopy entrance.

raw.Walkable blocks: Plaka/Anafiotika (Adrianou → Mnisikleous → the Cycladic whitewashed lanes under the north cliff, 1.2 km, 60 m ascent); Monastiraki/Psyrri (Ermou → Agiou Dimitriou → Sarri, 1.3 km); Koukaki (Dimitrakopoulou → Drakou → Veikou, 1.1 km flat, the best café density in the city); Exarchia (Themistokleous → Plateia Exarcheion → Strefi Hill, 1.4 km with a 50 m climb); Pangrati (Plateia Varnava → Arhimidous → the First Cemetery, 1.5 km); Kypseli (Fokionos Negri's 900 m linear park).
raw.Transit pass: the **Ath.ena Ticket** paper card or Ath.ena Card holds a **90-minute ticket at €1.20**, a **24-hour at €4.10**, a **5-day at €8.20** (none of which cover the airport), and a **3-day tourist ticket at €20.00** which does include one airport return. Contactless bank cards now work at gates for full-fare products.
raw.Airport transfer: **Metro Line 3** (blue) ATH → Syntagma, ~40 min, **€9 single / €16 return valid 30 days**; trains every 30 min from 06:30 to 23:30. **X95 express bus** to Syntagma runs 24 hours at **€5.50** and takes 60-90 min depending on traffic. Taxi is a fixed €40 daytime / €55 night to the centre.
raw.Booking timeline: the **Acropolis operates hourly timed slots** with a per-slot visitor cap, book on the official **hhticket.gr** portal 1-3 weeks ahead in spring and autumn, and take the **08:00 first slot**. The old €30 five-day combined state ticket was **discontinued in April 2025**; the €30 now buys the Acropolis alone, and other sites are ticketed separately or through private multi-site passes. **Acropolis Museum** and the **National Archaeological Museum** are same-day. Restaurants: Nolan and Seychelles want 5-10 days.
raw.Architectural focal points: Iktinos and Kallikrates's Parthenon (447-432 BC) and its entasis and inward-leaning columns; Mnesikles's Propylaia; the Erechtheion's Caryatid porch (originals in the museum, casts in situ); Hadrian's Library and the Tower of the Winds in the Roman Agora; the 11th-century cloisonné brickwork of Kapnikarea and the Little Metropolis; the Athenian Trilogy on Panepistimiou by Theophil and Christian Hansen (1859-85); Bernard Tschumi's 2009 Acropolis Museum with its glass-floored excavation; Renzo Piano's 2016 SNFCC under its sliding canopy.
raw.Eating structure: mezedopoleia and *koutoukia* for dinner across Psyrri, Pangrati and Exarchia; souvlaki and *koulouri* by day; one modern kitchen mid-week; a market morning at Varvakios. Old-school tavernas take walk-ins; the modern set requires booking.
raw.Day trip: **Cape Sounion** by **KTEL Attikis orange coach** from Pedion tou Areos / Mavromateon terminal, about 1h45 along the coastal road, roughly €7 each way, or **Aegina** by Hellenic Seaways ferry from Piraeus, 40 min by Flying Dolphin (~€18) or 70 min conventional (~€10-14).

sources.verified: Acropolis adult admission confirmed at **€30 year-round with hourly timed slots** and a 15-minute grace window either side; the official state reservation portal is **hhticket.gr**; the government's €30 five-day combined multi-site ticket was **discontinued in April 2025** and remaining "combo" products are private packages. OASA fares confirmed from the operator's own price list: 90-minute €1.20, 24-hour €4.10, 5-day €8.20, 3-day tourist ticket €20.00 including airport transfer, airport metro €9 one-way / €16 return valid 30 days, X95 express bus €5.50.
sources.confidenceNotes: Acropolis Museum (€15/€10) and National Archaeological Museum (€12/€6) seasonal pricing, and the individual site fees for the Ancient Agora, Kerameikos and Sounion, are 2025-26 figures revised each spring, re-verify. The Greek climate-resilience levy bands change by season and were last restructured in 2024; confirm current rates. KTEL Sounion coach fare and timetable, and Aegina ferry pricing, are approximate and seasonal. Summer midday Acropolis closures are weather-dependent and announced same-day. Restaurant booking lead times and Kostas's opening hours should be re-checked.
